text:
The headlines in Florida all week were about two names: Aleksander Barkov and Brad Marchand, both nearing a return, both listed as possible for Ottawa. They played, and the Panthers beat the Senators 5-3. Marchand had three assists in 14:12 and six shots on goal. Barkov, back after a long absence, scored the fifth goal on a 6% chance. If you were waiting for the Panthers to look like the Panthers, this was a decent first look.

It was not easy. Eetu Luostarinen put Florida ahead late in the first, and then Ottawa scored twice in 41 seconds early in the second: Dylan Cozens tipped an Artem Zub shot past Jacob Markstrom, and Philip Tomasino followed, both off Zub and Jake Sanderson. That pushed the Senators to 66% to win. Cozens has been on a run, with six goals and 12 points in his last 13 games, as Graeme Nichols noted. But Florida owned the rest of the period, out-chancing Ottawa 1.55 to 0.93 in expected goals (the quality of chances created). Niko Mikkola tipped in the tying goal, and Anton Lundell finished a 41% look at 18:55, the biggest swing of the game, taking Florida from 52% to 75%.

Sam Bennett's power-play goal early in the third came on a 90% chance, about as close to a sure thing as hockey offers, and Barkov's goal made it 5-2 before Michael Amadio scored late for Ottawa. The Senators went 0 for 5 on the power play, which is where this one slipped away; Florida went 1 for 2.

Neither goalie decided it. Markstrom stopped 25 of 28 and Linus Ullmark 27 of 31, both slightly better than their shots deserved. By shot quality, Florida wins this about 59% of the time, a reasonable reading of a close game the Panthers controlled when it mattered. Ottawa had won the October meeting 5-1. This time Florida had its full group.
headline: Barkov and Marchand come back, and Florida looks whole again
